docs.title: MagicArray – API Reference
docs.text: The MagicArray class provides a complete pedagogical implementation of array operations, enriched with benchmarking and visualization hooks. This page documents each method in detail, with usage examples and expected outputs.

docs.title: Class Signature
docs.text:
class MagicArray:
    def __init__(self, data=None):
        ...
  • Parameters
  • data (list, optional): Initial array contents. Can include integers, strings, objects, or nested structures.
  • Behavior
  • Initializes with dynamic capacity.
  • Supports expansion/shrinkage with overflow/underflow simulation.

docs.title: append(item)
docs.text:
Add an element to the end of the array.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.append(4)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 2, 3, 4]

docs.title: insert(index, item)
docs.text:
Insert an element at a specific position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([10, 20, 30])
arr.insert(1, 15)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[10, 15, 20, 30]

docs.title: delete(index)
docs.text:
Remove an element at a specific position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([5, 6, 7])
arr.delete(1)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[5, 7]

docs.title: get(index)
docs.text:
Retrieve element at position.

Example

arr = MagicArray(['a', 'b', 'c'])
print(arr.get(2))

Output

c

docs.title: set(index, item)
docs.text:
Update element at position.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.set(0, 99)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[99, 2, 3]

docs.title: linear_search(item)
docs.text:
Return index if found, else -1.

Example

arr = MagicArray([4, 8, 12])
print(arr.linear_search(8))

Output

1

docs.title: binary_search(item)
docs.text:
Return index if found (requires sorted array).

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 3, 5, 7, 9])
print(arr.binary_search(7))

Output

3

docs.title: traverse()
docs.text:
Return list of all elements.

Example

arr = MagicArray([100, 200, 300])
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[100, 200, 300]

docs.title: Sorting Algorithms
docs.text: Each sorting method returns a sorted array and records benchmarking metrics.

docs.title: bubble_sort()
docs.text:
Example

arr = MagicArray([9, 2, 5])
arr.bubble_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[2, 5, 9]

docs.title: quick_sort()
docs.text:
Example

arr = MagicArray([10, 7, 8, 9, 1])
arr.quick_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 7, 8, 9, 10]

docs.title: benchmark(algorithm)
docs.text:
Run algorithm and return metrics.

Example

arr = MagicArray([3, 1, 2])
metrics = arr.benchmark('bubble_sort')
print(metrics)

Output

{'algorithm': 'bubble_sort', 'time': 0.0001, 'comparisons': 3, 'swaps': 2}

docs.title: visualize()
docs.text:
Generate chart (PNG) of current array state.

Example

arr = MagicArray([4, 2, 7])
arr.visualize()

Output - Creates demo_int.png showing array contents.

docs.title: export(filename)
docs.text:
Save array contents to JSON/CSV.

Example

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.export("array.json")

Output - File array.json created with contents [1, 2, 3].

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
• IndexError → Raised for invalid index access.
  • ValueError → Raised for invalid operations (e.g., searching non‑comparable types).

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Open your terminal and run:

git clone https://github.com/AI-Alchemy-Hub/alchemy-magicstructures.git
cd alchemy-magicstructures

docs.title: Step 2: Local Editable Install
docs.text:
Install in editable mode so changes are reflected immediately:

pip install -e .

This will also install required dependencies: - NumPy ≥ 1.20 - Matplotlib ≥ 3.0

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Check that the package is installed:

pip list | findstr alchemy-magicstructures

Or test import in Python:

from alchemy_magicstructures import MagicArray
print("MagicArray ready!")

docs.title: Step 4: Run Demo Scripts
docs.text:
Try the examples provided:

python examples/magicarray_demo.py

Expected outcome: - A sample MagicArray is created. - Sorting algorithms run on test data. - PNG charts (demo_int.png, demo_str.png, etc.) are generated in the project root.

docs.title: Step 5: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• If dependencies are missing, reinstall: bash pip install numpy matplotlib
  • If using multiple Python versions, ensure you are running the correct interpreter (python3 vs python).
  • For Windows users, run commands in Git Bash or PowerShell.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
MagicArray is the foundational class in the Alchemy‑MagicStructures library. It is designed to help learners understand dynamic arrays and sorting algorithms through: - Core operations: insert, delete, update, search. - Sorting algorithms: bubble, insertion, selection, merge, quick. - Visualisation: automatic charts using Matplotlib. - Benchmarking: measure average run‑time of algorithms.

This class is the Milestone 1 (M1) deliverable in the course syllabus, serving as the entry point for exploring advanced data structures with practical examples.

docs.title: Why MagicArray?
docs.text: Most learners struggle to connect theory with practice. MagicArray bridges that gap by: - Providing hands‑on coding exercises. - Offering visual feedback (PNG charts). - Allowing performance comparisons between algorithms. - Serving as a foundation for later structures (stacks, queues, trees).

docs.title: Learning Goals
docs.text: By the end of this module, learners will: 1. Understand how arrays work internally. 2. Implement and test multiple sorting algorithms. 3. Visualise data transformations. 4. Benchmark algorithms for efficiency. 5. Prepare for more complex structures in future milestones.

docs.title: Python Environment
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher is required.
  • Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• NumPy ≥ 1.20 – for array handling and benchmarking.
  • Matplotlib ≥ 3.0 – for visualisation and chart generation.

These are installed automatically when you install the package.

docs.title: Basic Knowledge
docs.text: Learners should be comfortable with: - Python lists and indexing. - Comparison operators (<, >, ==). - Writing simple classes with __init__ and __lt__.

docs.title: MagicArray – Tutorials
docs.text: This tutorial walks through all the methods of the MagicArray class in a single consolidated flow. Follow each section step by step to practise construction, access, searching, sorting, benchmarking, and visualisation.

docs.title: Create and Append
docs.text:
from alchemy_magicstructures import MagicArray

arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.append(4)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 2, 3, 4]

docs.title: Insert and Delete
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([10, 20, 30])
arr.insert(1, 15)
arr.delete(2)
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[10, 15, 30]

docs.title: Get and Set
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray(['a', 'b', 'c'])
print(arr.get(1))   # → b
arr.set(1, 'z')
print(arr.traverse())

Output

b
['a', 'z', 'c']

docs.title: Linear Search
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([4, 8, 12])
print(arr.linear_search(8))

Output

1

docs.title: Binary Search
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 3, 5, 7, 9])
print(arr.binary_search(7))

Output

3

docs.title: Traverse
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([100, 200, 300])
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[100, 200, 300]

docs.title: Bubble Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([9, 2, 5])
arr.bubble_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[2, 5, 9]

docs.title: Selection Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([64, 25, 12, 22, 11])
arr.selection_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[11, 12, 22, 25, 64]

docs.title: Insertion Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([5, 2, 9, 1])
arr.insertion_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 2, 5, 9]

docs.title: Merge Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([38, 27, 43, 3, 9, 82, 10])
arr.merge_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[3, 9, 10, 27, 38, 43, 82]

docs.title: Quick Sort
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([10, 7, 8, 9, 1])
arr.quick_sort()
print(arr.traverse())

Output

[1, 7, 8, 9, 10]

docs.title: Measure Algorithm Performance
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([3, 1, 2])
metrics = arr.benchmark('bubble_sort')
print(metrics)

Output

{'algorithm': 'bubble_sort', 'time': 0.0001, 'comparisons': 3, 'swaps': 2}

docs.title: Generate Chart
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([4, 2, 7])
arr.visualise()

Output - Creates demo_int.png showing array contents.

docs.title: Export Data
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
arr.export("array.json")

Output - File array.json created with contents [1, 2, 3].

docs.title: IndexError
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 2])
try:
    arr.get(5)
except IndexError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

Output

Error: Invalid index access

docs.title: ValueError
docs.text:
arr = MagicArray([1, 2, 3])
try:
    arr.linear_search({'x': 1})
except ValueError as e:
    print("Error:", e)

Output

Error: Unsupported comparison type

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
This tutorial demonstrated: - Construction and access methods (append, insert, delete, get, set). - Searching (linear_search, binary_search) and traversal. - Sorting algorithms (bubble, selection, insertion, merge, quick). - Benchmarking performance. - Visualisation and export. - Exception handling.

With this single consolidated tutorial, learners can practise every method of the MagicArray class end‑to‑end.
